audit_findings.title: Convertible shares and owner earnings represent inconsistent claims
audit_findings.magnitude: Up to 5.977 million shares, or 11.2% of the 53.530 million denominator; removing all raises value per share 12.6%, including base from $33.52 to $37.73 and bull from $38.80 to $43.68
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator assumes full conversion-share dilution while equity-level OE retains note interest and the bridge recognizes neither cash-settled principal nor the capped-call offset.
audit_findings.evidence: Upon conversion, the Company will pay cash up to the aggregate principal amount of the notes to be converted and pay or deliver, as the case may be, cash, common stock or a combination of cash and common stock, at the Company’s election, in respect of the remainder, if any, of the Company’s conversion obligation in excess of the aggregate principal amount of the notes being converted.
audit_findings.explanation: The claim inconsistency is demonstrated, although the precise net-share dilution requires the conversion and capped-call calculations. Even the maximum favorable correction leaves the bull value at $43.68, 57.6% below the $102.92 market price, so it cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild diluted shares under net-share settlement at each scenario value, including capped-call offsets, and rerun per-share values without changing OE; alternatively use an if-converted numerator and matching denominator.

audit_findings.title: Recurring capitalized software investment may bypass owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed scale is $6.7 million of capitalized marketed-software costs plus an $18.4 million ERP asset-balance increase, totaling $25.1 million, or 22.5% of the $111.8 million anchor; if entirely omitted, the computed base-case effect is approximately $352.7 million or $6.59 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized software and cloud-implementation cash investment can avoid current earnings expense and may also fall outside the PP&E capex deduction, causing OE and every projected cash flow derived from the anchor to be overstated.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company capitalized $ 6.7 million and $ 7.7 million in software development costs for ongoing initiatives during fiscal 2026 and 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The recurring capitalized expenditures are demonstrated, but their omission from OE is not. Their filed scale is large relative to the anchor and could reduce the base equity estimate by about 19.7% if none was captured, materially changing the valuation range and buy-below level even though it would reinforce the conclusion that the shares are expensive at $102.92.
audit_findings.action: Trace FY2026 marketed-software additions and ERP implementation cash payments through the OE reconciliation and cash-flow classifications; deduct any uncaptured maintenance investment and rerun all scenarios and the margin-of-safety price.

audit_findings.title: The FY2026 anchor does not fully represent the current Vivasure perimeter
audit_findings.mechanism: The anchor includes only the short post-acquisition period, while projected OE and growth apply to a business that owns Vivasure for full periods and bears its commercialization costs, investment requirements and any resulting revenue.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 9, 2026, the Company acquired all of the outstanding equity interests of Vivasure Medical Limited (“Vivasure”) for a net purchase price of $ 164.4 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated: Vivasure was acquired on January 9, 2026 and contributed nominal FY2026 revenue. The filings do not separately disclose enough post-acquisition revenue, expenses or investment to measure a normalized OE adjustment. Continuing costs could lower value, while successful commercialization could raise future OE and growth.
audit_findings.action: Obtain standalone monthly or quarterly Vivasure revenue, operating expenses, capitalized development, working-capital needs and regulatory spending from acquisition through the latest quarter; construct a full-year perimeter adjustment and rerun the anchor and growth cases.

audit_findings.title: Acquisition earn-outs are an unbridged senior cash claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $21.016 million at June 27, 2026, equal to $0.39 per valuation share and 1.2% of the $1.794 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: The valuation adds cash in the equity bridge but does not deduct the acquisition-related contingent-consideration liability owed ahead of common equity.
audit_findings.evidence: The fair value of contingent consideration associated with acquisitions was $ 21.1 million and $ 2.3 million as of March 28, 2026 and March 29, 2025, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The bridge omission is demonstrated. Deducting the entire latest filed fair value would reduce base value from $33.52 to about $33.13 per share and would not affect the conclusion relative to the $102.92 market price.
audit_findings.action: Deduct the June 27, 2026 contingent-consideration balance from the bridge unless the modeled OE explicitly includes settlement cash flows; confirm that subsequent payments or remeasurements are not counted twice.

audit_findings.title: The anchor may retain a nonrecurring acquisition remeasurement gain
audit_findings.magnitude: $4.9 million pretax; $3.724 million using the filed 24.0% FY2026 tax rate, producing an approximately $52.3 million or $0.98-per-share base-case effect if fully retained
audit_findings.mechanism: A one-time acquisition gain retained in FY2026 OE inflates the anchor and therefore the forecast-period cash flows and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: During fiscal 2026, the Company recorded a gain of $ 4.9 million within interest and other expense, net on the consolidated statements of income as a result of the remeasurement of the Company’s prior equity interest of approximately 30 % in Vivasure, which had a fair value of $ 47.3 million.
audit_findings.explanation: The $4.9 million gain is demonstrated, but its retention in the OE reconciliation is unresolved. Even if fully retained and removed at the filed annual tax rate, the computed base value reduction is about 2.9%, from $33.52 to approximately $32.54 per share, which cannot change the current valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace interest and other expense through the FY2026 OE reconciliation; remove the after-tax Vivasure remeasurement gain if retained and separately test whether the $1.879 million contingent-consideration remeasurement benefit was normalized.

audit_findings.title: The unfunded pension position is another claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $11.181 million gross funded deficit at March 28, 2026, or $0.21 per valuation share; approximately $3.881 million or $0.07 per share after the separately reported $7.3 million reinsurance asset
audit_findings.mechanism: An accumulated pension deficit is a claim ahead of common equity that may require a bridge deduction unless its future funding is already captured in OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Substantially all of the unfunded status is non-current.
audit_findings.explanation: The funded deficit and absence of an explicit bridge deduction are demonstrated. Even the conservative gross deduction is only 0.6% of the $1.794 billion base equity value and reduces base value from $33.52 to about $33.31 per share; recognizing the reinsurance asset makes the effect smaller.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the latest funded status, tax effect, plan-specific reinsurance asset and whether projected OE captures deficit-funding contributions; deduct only the resulting unprovided net claim.
